bull_bear.body:
- Established brand and reputation in Indian paper markets
- Strategic presence in high-growth tissue and copier segments
- Captive agro-forestry plantation program (16,491 acres added in FY26) securing wood supply and supporting sustainability
- Integrated chemical business providing internal chlorine dioxide and external caustic soda sales, reducing input cost volatility
- Advanced Process Control (APC) implementation yielding ~12% reduction in specific chlorine dioxide consumption
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Raw material sourcing cost inflation and supply disruption due to regulatory restrictions — Transit permit restrictions on wood movement in Madhya Pradesh led to ~7% higher sourcing cost and impacted fibre yield; though partially reversed, such policy changes create recurring cost and quality risks.
- Pricing pressure from imports and domestic overcapacity — Writing & Printing paper prices dropped ~4% due to nil-duty imports and sluggish tenders; tissue prices fell ~7.5% as the market absorbed new capacity, squeezing margins despite record volumes.
- Margin compression from inability to offset external headwinds — Operational gains and small-scale high-impact projects were insufficient to counter pricing declines and government-driven sourcing cost increases, leading to squeezed operating margins.
- Regulatory and policy risk affecting cost structure — Government policies inflating sourcing-side costs (e.g., transit permit rules) directly impact profitability, and GST reforms affecting the notebook segment add demand-side uncertainty.
- Technology and capex execution risk in shifting product mix — The new tissue line capex project aims to de-commoditize the product mix, but delays, cost overruns, or failure to achieve value-added penetration could impair expected profitability improvement.
- Environmental compliance risk in Caustic Soda business — The Caustic Soda business missed its GHG target set by MoEFCC, creating potential regulatory exposure or cost if carbon market mechanisms impose penalties or require credit purchases.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: The Company manufactures Writing & Printing paper, tissue products, and caustic soda/chlor-alkali chemicals. It serves domestic institutional, corporate, and retail customers across education, FMCG, pharmaceuticals, e-commerce, hospitality, and healthcare, with exports to UAE and other markets. Operations are supported by in-house agro-forestry for wood pulp and a chemical plant that supplies internal and external demand.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Paper & Tissue:** Writing & Printing paper, Copier paper, Tissue products (facial tissues, kitchen towels), Colour tissues, Bamboo-rich tissues
- **Chemicals:** Caustic soda lye, Chlorine dioxide (captive use)

- Captive agro-forestry plantation program (16,491 acres added in FY26) securing wood supply and supporting sustainability
- Integrated chemical business providing internal chlorine dioxide and external caustic soda sales, reducing input cost volatility

business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Deepen engagement with micro-markets through Hub Meets and the Orient Stars digital platform, widen presence across new product categories such as bamboo and colour tissue, and strengthen offerings across growing segments like health and hygiene, copier, and sustainable products.
- Embark on a business-excellence journey ('Project SANKALP') to address weaknesses and threats, with five key improvement areas taken up as daily themes for data-driven discussions and fast-tracked decisions, complemented by an idea-generation drive ('Urja-Mitra').
- Maintain commitment to achieving net neutrality targets in both carbon and water footprints, expand plantation coverage, implement Good Agricultural Practices, and sustain the proportion of renewables in the energy mix at ~40%.
- Continue digital transformation through state-of-the-art Advanced Process Control (APC) to reduce specific consumption of inputs like Chlorine Dioxide in the bleaching process.
- The Company has a Dividend Distribution Policy approved by the Board, available on its website, in compliance with Regulation 43A of the Listing Regulations.
- Commitment to achieving net neutrality targets in both carbon and water footprints.
- Expanded plantation coverage by 16,491 acres and implemented Good Agricultural Practices across 5,400 acres, benefiting 3,540 families.
- Maintained ~40% proportion of renewables in the energy mix.
- Achieved ~12% reduction in specific consumption of Chlorine Dioxide in bleaching process via Advanced Process Control.
- Paper business outperformed its GHG target set by MoEFCC; Company-level net effect may yield surplus carbon credits as National Carbon Market formalizes.
- Helped build more than 1,280 water harvesting structures across the local community, capable of harvesting up to 32 billion liters of water.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company has initiated a capex project for installing a new Tissue line. This capital infusion shall bring in state-of-art technology to Orient Paper and help it stay relevant in today's markets by expanding its product basket and improving its profitability. This shall de-commoditize the Company's product mix and shift it towards value-added categories. The Company continued to invest towards the upkeep of its assets with a capex of ~ Rs 52 crores in FY26.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Indian paper industry volume growth estimated at ~5-6% during CY2024-26, driven by favorable demographics, rising literacy, increasing packaging demand, and a shift towards organized and value-added segments.
- Tissue paper market experiencing strong growth of 10-15%, driven by rising hygiene awareness, urbanization, disposable incomes, and institutional demand from hospitality, healthcare, airports, and food delivery.
- Writing & Printing segment growing at ~2-3% CAGR, with copier paper as the fastest-growing sub-category at ~5-6% CAGR, supported by corporate usage, educational institutions, and the services sector; 30-40% incremental demand from NEP.
- Caustic soda demand growing at a healthy CAGR of ~6-7% over FY22-25, supported by rising demand across alumina, textiles, pulp & paper, and chemicals.
- Raw material sourcing cost under pressure due to transit permit effects in Madhya Pradesh, though eased towards the latter part of FY26 when the state government removed Eucalyptus from the list of products requiring Transit Permit.
- Average paper prices dropped by ~6% over FY25, with W&P segment down ~4% due to rising imports at nil duty, sluggish tender orders, and GST reforms; Tissue segment down ~7.5% due to time-lag in absorbing capacity increase.
- Value-added products represented ~55% of the overall product mix, with product mix comprising 62% Writing & Printing paper and 38% tissue products.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers
